So what

✓So what

Three questions set your path

Organizer checks

Only sanctioned results count. SGF-run events are sanctioned automatically. IP events take five steps, all others three

2C.1.12C.1.2

!So what

Bring SGF in before you sign

Organizer submits

Submit the draft contract and the owner’s authorization through the SGF website. SGF can support the negotiation

2C.1.3

!So what

Four tests, all must pass

SGF decides

Calendar fit, transparent negotiation, national image and alignment with SGF objectives. Sign only once approved

2C.1.3

!So what

The form is your rulebook

Organizer submits

Nine sections, six of them the standards you commit to. Declare the fee, none for amateur events, and request date protection

2C.1.42C.1.5

!So what

Approval locks your date

SGF decides

SGF confirms the date, protects it on request and invoices the fee. A rejection can be appealed

2C.1.6

!So what

Deliver what you signed

Organizer delivers

Below the agreed standards, fines of up to SAR 10,000 apply, doubled on repeat. Delivery is set out in 2C.2

2C.1.6

!So what

No results, no ranking

Organizer submits

Verify the scores, then submit to SGF and to rankings such as WAGR. Only then are results recognized nationally

2C.1.6
Throughout

!Compliance · all year, through the venue license

The venue pays for the breach

Hosting without approval costs SAR 30,000 to 120,000 per breach and a hosting ban. Organizers secure every approval first; venues verify them before agreeing to host

2C.1.7
Note: The 15-month timing is derived from the 12-month application deadline and the 90-day hosting decision. 2C.2 Delivery and officiating - executive summary: one organizer is accountable end to end, and national approvals gate every stage

✓Guidance!Mandatory where flagged
Back
1Riyadh Golf Club at dusk, before tournament week
PrepareMonths before, to event week

Approvals take longer than set-up, so the clock starts 12 months out

What it takes

  • Twelve plans, cleared by four authorities: SGF, the Ministry of Health, the municipality and Civil Defense
  • One accountable lead per operational area; referees appointed by SGF, volunteers drawn from one SGF-cleared pool

What is at stake

Without the national approvals the gates do not open, whatever the sanctioning status

2Live play at Royal Greens Golf & Country Club, KAEC
DeliverTournament days

Referees settle play, safety is non-negotiable, the rest is conduct

What it takes

  • Referees’ rulings are final; marshals keep spectators silent behind the ropes and media within the access rules
  • Medical cover scales with attendance to the Ministry of Health minimum; the siren stops play when weather threatens

What is at stake

Fall below the agreed standards and the venue is fined; a serious incident goes to SGF at once

Deep dive: spectator and media etiquette
3LIV Golf Invitational Jeddah 2022, Royal Greens
ReportAfter the event

The event is not over until SGF has the results and the file

What it takes

  • Verified results to SGF and to rankings such as WAGR within 48 hours
  • Incident reports, the medical file and a final report within 30 days, and volunteers rated within a week

What is at stake

Late results do not count for rankings, and poor volunteer ratings can weigh on the next application

1organizer, accountable end to end
8operational areas, one lead each
12plans before the event
37roles, 15 open to volunteers
48 hto file the official results
30 daysto close the final report

2C.2.5 Around the course - spectators watch quietly from behind the ropes, and media work within set access and recording rules

✓Guidance
Back
1Prepare2C.2.1 to 2C.2.32Deliver2C.2.4 to 2C.2.63Report2C.2.7
What this page settles

Six conduct standards apply to spectators and to media, each backed by graduated sanctions

1Spectator etiquettePlay is observed from behind the ropes, in silence
2Media etiquetteCoverage requires accreditation, without disturbing play
1Spectator etiquette✓Guidance

Spectators watch quietly from behind the ropes, and never interfere with play

PositionBehind the ropes, about 25 m away; cross where marshals direct; off tees and greens
During a strokeStill and silent until the group has played; applaud good play, never a mistake
PlayersNo advice to players; autographs only after the round, where designated
Ball and courseNever touch a ball or club; stay out of cordoned areas; use the bins
Phones and recordingSilent phones and calls away from play; no flash, video or live posts
Conduct and safetyFollow marshals; react at once to “Fore” and the siren; no heckling or abuse
EnforcementRising with the breach
1Course removalDisruptive behavior
2Grounds removalRepeat breach, no refund
3Future banOrganizer’s discretion
2Media etiquette✓Guidance

Accredited media work inside the ropes without disturbing play

PositionInside the ropes only with that day’s credential, within arm’s length of the ropes
During a strokeSilent shutters; never on a tee or in a player’s line; move when asked
PlayersInterviews only after the scorecard is signed, with consent; never in the scoring area
EquipmentNo flash, tripods, ladders, drones or carts on the course
Recording and postingNo video of live play except the licensed broadcaster; no hole-by-hole posts
Conduct and accessCredential visible and not transferable; follow staff instructions
EnforcementRising with the breach
1Content takedownPosts or footage
2Credential revokedFor the person
3Outlet revokedFor the whole outlet
Note: SGF sets four spectator rules: outside the ropes, silent during shots, never touch a ball, and shelter at the siren. All other rules are recommended practice. Crowd management is part of the plans in 2C.2.1, marshals in 2C.2.4, and media rights in 2D.1.7Source: Saudi Golf Federation (spectator etiquette); The R&A (The Open spectator code of conduct); USGA (Championships spectator conduct policy; media credential regulations); European Golf Association (spectator policy); PGA TOUR (fan codes of conduct; World Wide Technology Championship spectator etiquette; Media Regulations, 2026); The R&A and USGA (Rules of Golf)
